text:
Devon Levi made 39 saves on 40 shots, and that is why a game LAK controlled ended 4-1 for EDM. The Kings out-attempted the Oilers 80 to 37 and held a 2.94 to 2.19 edge in expected goals, which gives them a 72 percent chance to win if the shots were replayed. Levi stopped 1.94 goals more than the chances against him called for, and Brandt Clarke's wrist shot in the second period, a 3 percent look, was the only puck to beat him.

EDM did its damage in a first-period burst with the chances they got. Leon Draisaitl scored at 7:16 on a snap shot, and Vasily Podkolzin followed on the power play at 8:16 to make it 2-0. Connor McDavid added a backhand at 15:48 for a 3-0 lead. LAK goalie Anton Forsberg stopped all nine shots he faced before Darcy Kuemper took over, and Kuemper allowed three goals on seven shots, 2.11 more than those shots deserved.

The Kings pushed hardest in the second, out-chancing EDM 1.66 to 0.34 in expected goals. Drew Doughty had a 22 percent look that Levi turned away, and Clarke finally broke through at 17:29. Podkolzin put it away at 17:42 of the third with his second goal, a wrist shot on a 50 percent chance. McDavid finished with a goal and three assists on 21:36 of ice time and took first star.
